source: Reliance Industries Limited - Half-Yearly EC Compliance Report, Jamnagar (reporting period 01 Apr - 30 Sep 2024)
notes: Evidence: newly identified in Phase 3 step 2, Condition 12 (Marine/Coastal) under Proposal No. J.11011/232/2005-IA-II (I) ('Environmental clearance for expansion and modernization of petrochemical refinery complex', entity Reliance Industries Limited, filed from Village Meghpar/Padana, Tehsil Lalpur, Jamnagar - a village pairing that RIL's own postal/pincode registrations (e.g. 'M/S RELIANCE INDUSTRIES LIMITED UNIT OF RELIANCE JAMNAGAR SEZ VILLAGE MEGAPAR PADANA TALUKA LALPUR DIST JAMNAGAR') identify as the Reliance Jamnagar SEZ site) states: 'The extension of the existing tank farm shall be designed in such a way that the residual flow including floor washing do not percolate to the marine areas. RIL's own compliance response states: 'The augmentation and expansion of the marine facilities has been carried out in consultation with NIO.' Establishes: this EC proposal, which reports a combined 59.7 MMTPA 'Crude Oil Processing Capacity' (Production Capacity table, same proposal), names crude-handling SPMs (not only product SPMs) among the marine facilities being expanded for this capacity. 59.7 MMTPA is consistent with combining the original refinery's then-capacity of 27 MMTPA (this same compiled filing's Proposal No. J-11011/25/93-IA-II (I), 'processing capacity from 18 to 27 MMTPA') with the Jamnagar Export Refinery Project (JERP)/SEZ refinery's separately reported 580 Kbpsd crude capacity (this same filing's Proposal No. J-11011/149/2007-IA-II (I), production capacity table entry 'Jamnagar Export Refinery (JERP) (already under implementation) ... 580' Kbpsd crude), i.e. this proposal's reported capacity is the DTA+SEZ complex total, not the DTA refinery alone. The endpoint is matched to R023 because PPAC publishes it as 'RPL (SEZ), Jamnagar' under RELIANCE INDUSTRIES LIMITED in GUJARAT - a company-and-project-history match, not a location guess. CORROBORATION: Gujarat Maritime Board's captive-jetty register (SRC010, already the source for PORT016 and for NL022) lists every Sikka SPM/berth under a single operator, 'M/s Reliance Ports & Terminal Ltd.' (SPM Nos. 3, 4, 5, two further SBMs, a 4th tanker berth and a 5th product-jetty berth), with no entry anywhere distinguishing a separate DTA-only or SEZ-only Reliance marine facility - i.e. RPTL/Sikka is documented as Reliance's one shared marine terminal at Jamnagar, not two. This is also consistent with Reliance Jamnagar Infrastructure Limited's 2009 EIA (SRC041, data/raw/ril/eia_jamnagar_sez_2009-10.txt), which states the SEZ/JERP refinery's seawater is drawn 'as in the case of the existing refinery' through 'the existing seawater intake provided at the marine terminal area' - the same single marine terminal, not a separate one. CAVEATS: (1) Condition 12 itself does not name Sikka or Vadinar; the locality match to PORT016 rests on RPTL/Sikka being the only Reliance-operated crude-capable marine facility documented anywhere in this project's sources for Jamnagar, corroborated by the GMB register cited above. (2) The 59.7 MMTPA capacity match to DTA(27)+SEZ(~33, from 580 Kbpsd) is an arithmetic inference across three proposals in the same compiled filing, not a sentence in the source stating the equality outright. (3) GMB's register does not itself label any specific RPTL SPM as crude vs. product, so which of RPTL's several Sikka SPMs is/are the crude SPMs is not resolved by this edge; the edge asserts the crude supply relationship and shared-facility operator only, not a specific SPM unit. This supersedes the Phase 3 step 1 finding recorded against SRC040, which examined only the two original-refinery proposals and the dedicated SEZ proposal for marine/crude conditions and did not identify this combined-complex proposal's Condition 12; see the corrected SRC040 registry note and docs/data_sources.md / docs/network_connectivity_report.md for the full account.
